cohort: 8,211,850 pregnancies ending in live births or stillbirths in England from 1997 to 2012
finding: Hyperemesis gravidarum (HG) is associated with increased odds of various adverse maternal outcomes like anaemia, preeclampsia, and thromboembolism, and while associated with decreased odds of stillbirth and post-term delivery, it is also linked to increased odds of preterm delivery, cesarean section, and neonatal complications.
mod_finding: Women with HG were more likely to have a cesarean section (OR 1.12, 99% CI 1.08, 1.16).
